statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is 18% in the low band while Stress is elevated at 50%.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON. The only interval in the horizon that reaches the watch band is the 19:00Z-20:15Z quadruple-witching settlement window, which is described as a narrow mechanical-flow checkpoint rather than a session-wide condition. headline: Cash NDX 29,377.78 is pinned on its 29,371.89 session low after a failed bounce, but NQ 29,707.50 holds mid-band with SOX +1.06% and VIX 15.39 diverging, while the 10-year at 5.01% is the single aligned headwind into quadruple-witching settlement
body: Nasdaq-100 cash trades 29,377.78, down 0.23% against a 29,446.98 previous close and sitting directly on a 29,371.89 session low, after opening at 29,529.64 and running to a 29,560.30 high. Nasdaq-100 E-mini futures print 29,707.50, down 0.12%, inside a 29,648.00-29,966.75 band. The structural question for this score is whether the tape is producing the persistent no-retracement path that overwhelms mean reversion, and the observed evidence says it is not, which is why Tail stays in the low band even though the index is at its lows. The day has produced a complete two-way rotation: the cash session opened higher, extended, failed, sold through to 29,407.28, recovered into positive territory and has now given that recovery back to make a marginal new low. That is one failed retracement, not repeated extension after failed retracements, and the entire cash range spans 188 points or about 0.64%. Futures remain 60 points above their own session low and 259 points below the overnight high at 29,966.75, which has now stood unretaken for roughly nine hours. The opening-auction continuation pattern that preceded the strategy's worst historical sessions did not appear today. Tail is lifted two points from the prior hour to acknowledge that the bounce failed and cash is pressing its low, and no further, because the amplifier stack required for a higher reading is absent. Cross-assets conflict rather than align. The PHLX Semiconductor Index trades 11,722.58, up 1.06%, while the index it dominates is lower on the day, a rotation divergence that reduces directional conviction without adding path risk. VIX at 15.39 is marginally lower in a 14.99-15.61 range against a 17.71 previous close, so the post-decision volatility crush remains intact and is not confirming the drift lower. Crude has eased for a third consecutive session, with WTI near 101.3 dollars and Brent near 104.3 dollars, both down about half a percent, as Saudi Arabia signalled it can restore partial East-West pipeline capacity within days and route some cargoes via Oman; US crude briefly traded below 100 dollars. That removes a stress channel that was firming an hour ago. The genuine headwind is rates: the 10-year yield is 5.01%, up about 7 basis points, and the 2-year is 4.75%, both sitting on the levels that have framed equity risk appetite since Wednesday's increase in the target range to 3.75-4.00% with a further increase signalled this year. H.15 put the 2-year and 10-year constant maturities at 4.74% and 5.01% on 16 September. Two US releases printed this morning and both were soft: August industrial production was unchanged on the month with manufacturing output down 0.3% and capacity utilisation at 76.3%, and the Conference Board Leading Economic Index receded 0.1% to 99.5. Soft data against a tightening policy path produces dispersion rather than direction, which is the definition of the mixed dominant mode carried here. The identified conditional risk for the rest of the session is mechanical rather than informational. September quadruple-witching settles at the 20:00Z cash close, and closing-auction volume on these dates historically runs several times a normal session. Concentrated expiration and pin flow can briefly overwhelm mean reversion, which is why the danger window is drawn narrowly at 19:00Z-20:15Z rather than across the whole afternoon, and why only the 19:00Z and 20:00Z forecast hours reach the watch band. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read at the start of this run but carried a 11:53Z collection time, roughly 278 minutes old, with partial coverage and no futures or calendar section, so it was treated as unhealthy and this assessment rests entirely on independently verified primary sources. Beyond the 21:00Z futures close the tape is shut until the Sunday reopen, so every later forecast hour describes a dormant market in which no price path can develop and the residual score covers weekend gap risk alone.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 published hours cover a complete transition. Thursday afternoon ran with Tail in the 20-24 watch band and a trend-up mode as the post-decision relief rally extended, with Stress decaying from 51% toward the mid-40s as the volatility crush progressed. From 22:00Z the assessment moved to green with a normal mode and Tail in the 17-18 area through the Asian and European sessions. Tail ticked to 19% during the European morning as futures firmed, then eased to 15-17% from 11:00Z once the overnight high was left behind and the mode was reclassified to mixed. Stress has held in the upper 40s to low 50s through the European and US hours, reflecting the yield and crude backdrop rather than realised index volatility.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the low band at 18-19% through the remainder of the US cash afternoon, on the condition that the narrow two-way band behaviour observed so far persists, then lifts it to 22% and 21% for the 19:00Z and 20:00Z hours containing the September quadruple-witching settlement, where concentrated mechanical expiration flow rather than new information is the identified risk. Those two hours are the only part of the horizon reaching the watch band and the only interval covered by the danger window. From 21:00Z the futures session closes for the week, so Tail falls to 10% and then toward a 5-7% structural floor across the closed weekend hours, while Stress decays into the low band and Confidence declines steadily with distance from the last observed price path. The horizon ends on Saturday afternoon, roughly 31 hours before the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, so the next assessment covering tradable structure will be rebuilt on freshly observed evidence.
